I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, this is still the most dependable way for me to use the full year, spread my risk, and match the tools and habits I already know well. I am 60, so I will not chase crops that need too much hand labor or market gambling. I will finish the winter wheat already on the land, manage it steadily with water and fertilizer, then after harvest I will move straight into summer maize so I do not lose soil moisture or the growing window.

For the wheat, I will stay with improved seed because it is more stable than old seed and less risky than trying something unfamiliar. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive fertilizer, because I want steady yield and lower waste. I will irrigate at the key times, mainly around jointing and grain filling, and I will control disease, weeds, and aphids with a few targeted sprays. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid summer maize because hybrid maize gives me better yield and stronger stand. I will use no-tillage for maize after wheat so I can sow quickly, save labor, and keep moisture in the field. I will give maize enough nitrogen to support ears, with balanced phosphorus and potassium, and I will irrigate if the summer rain is not enough. This is the plan I would follow because it is practical, familiar, and gives me the best chance of a stable income.
